findings.evidence: getZestIconElement uses `if (name in ZEST_ICON_ELEMENTS)`, which walks the prototype chain. Through the built package, <ZestIcon name="__proto__" /> throws "Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {})"; name="toString" and name="constructor" resolve to Object.prototype functions and log React warnings while rendering an empty <span class="zestIcon">. The only unknown-name test (ZestIcon.test.tsx:50-58) uses "not-a-real-icon", which is not on the prototype, so it passes.
findings.description: R5 says an unknown name renders nothing and does not throw, and documentation/examples.md:358 and the API docs promise this. A consumer passing an untrusted string as ZestIcon name can crash the render tree. Guard the lookup with Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(ZEST_ICON_ELEMENTS, name) or use a Map/null-prototype object, and add tests for "__proto__", "constructor", "toString" and "hasOwnProperty".

findings.evidence: The code examples at documentation/examples.md:123 and :180 use `import { ZestButtonConfigProvider, ZestButton, ZestIcon } from 'jattac.libs.web.zest-button'`, but the package has no named `ZestButton` export: UI/ZestButton.tsx:457 only default-exports it, UI/index.ts:1-2 re-exports only the default, and the built dist/index.cjs.js exports are default, ZestIcon, ZestButtonConfigProvider and useZestButtonConfig. The R7 docs tests (ZestIcon.test.tsx:117-136) only assert substrings, so no test compiles a snippet and the broken import ships.
findings.description: R7 requires every code example to compile against the new types; these examples do not compile. Change both imports to a default `ZestButton` import, and add a test that extracts the documented snippets and type-checks/renders them (the toggle feature has a type-check precedent at ZestButtonToggle.test.tsx:523, but it uses a hand-written object rather than the actual snippets).

findings.evidence: The table row for `settings` says the icon is "Sliders", but UI/zestIcons.tsx:96 draws a centre circle and a four-way cross (a target/crosshair), not sliders. The R7 table test (ZestIcon.test.tsx:104-115) extracts only the first column, so it cannot fail if the Icon, Variant, Button style, Icon side or Default behaviour columns are wrong; the settings mismatch passes.
findings.description: Correct the `settings` drawing or its description, and extend the table test to compare the icon description, variant, button style, icon side and default behaviour against semanticTypeButtonConfigDefaults. Advisory: documentation content is checked by review, and the reviewer already blocks the settings mismatch under DOC-001.

findings.evidence: ZestIcon is imported from "../UI/ZestIcon" in every test; no test imports it from "../UI" or the package root. The R5 acceptance "import { ZestIcon } from the package" and "does not remove or rename any existing export of UI/index.ts" therefore are not guarded: deleting UI/index.ts:4-5 or an existing export leaves the suite green. The built dist currently does export ZestIcon, so the present artifact is fine, but the source barrel regression would pass CI.
findings.description: Add one consumer-style test that imports ZestIcon, ZestIconProps, ZestIconSize, the default ZestButton, ZestButtonConfigProvider and useZestButtonConfig from "../UI", then renders a ZestIcon as a ZestButton iconLeft. This is blocking because the acceptance explicitly requires the package import and no test would fail if the barrel export regressed.

findings.evidence: The "each of the 28 new names is accepted by the SemanticType type" test only declares the literals in a SemanticType[] and asserts the array length. It never augments CustomZestSemanticTypes. If `keyof CustomZestSemanticTypes` were removed from the union at ZestButton.tsx:20, this test would still compile and pass; the R1 acceptance "still accepts the names added through CustomZestSemanticTypes" has no test.
findings.description: Add a small declaration file/test that augments `CustomZestSemanticTypes` with e.g. `publish: 'publish'` and assigns `'publish'` to SemanticType, mirroring the docs recipe at examples.md:167. Advisory because the union still ends in `keyof CustomZestSemanticTypes` today.

findings.evidence: The all-47 rendering test checks the label and that a button svg exists, but never spies on console.error. The R1 acceptance also says "and no console error"; a React warning or error on any of the 28 new types would not fail the loop. The fail-state test spies on console.error elsewhere (line 414), so the pattern exists.
findings.description: Wrap the ALL_TYPES render loop with a console.error spy and assert it was not called (restore afterwards). Advisory: this is a stronger assertion on an already-tested render path.

findings.evidence: The "next ... flips correctly for right-to-left pages" test only asserts child order and that the stylesheet has `.content { display: inline-flex }`. It never renders inside `dir="rtl"` or checks logical margins; DOM order alone is direction-agnostic. The R2 edge case is therefore not actually exercised.
findings.description: Render the next button inside a `dir="rtl"` container and assert the icon remains visually after the label (e.g. order/margin logic or computed direction), or assert the CSS uses logical properties. Advisory because inline-flex already mirrors in RTL and the mechanism is present.

findings.evidence: The shared-style test covers all 47 types with stroke=currentColor. The "follow the text colour" acceptance also names light, dark and system themes and every variant/button style, but tests render only the filled success/danger icons (line 346); outline/text/dashed and explicit light/dark/system icon renders are not checked. The currentColor mechanism is the same for all, so this is coverage breadth, not an uncovered behaviour.
findings.description: Optionally add a small matrix (a few variants/styles x light/dark/system) asserting the icon still uses currentColor and its variant text-colour variable. Advisory: the mechanism is already proven for every type.

findings.evidence: The "focus ring visible on every built-in type in light and dark themes" test only adds force-light/force-dark classes and regex-checks the stylesheet for `.button:focus-visible` and `--zest-focus-ring`; it never focuses a button. jsdom cannot compute :focus-visible, so the assertion proves the rule exists, not that a keyboard user sees it.
findings.description: Focus a representative button and assert the focus-visible class/selector path, or document that the CSS rule is the contract. Advisory: the shared button focus rule is not changed by this feature.

findings.evidence: The R6 documentation check only asserts that breaking-changes.md contains "Version 1.7.0". The required explanation that built-in icons are now library SVGs (breaking-changes.md:23-25) could be deleted and the test would still pass.
findings.description: Assert the icon-change heading/paragraph in breaking-changes.md, e.g. that it mentions library/inline SVG and Font Awesome. Advisory: the content is present today and the version check passes.

findings.evidence: packagePeerDependencies.test.ts only reads and asserts the react/react-dom ranges. findings.description: Add an assertion that package.json peerDependencies contains react-icons (and optionally that its bounds are unchanged). Advisory: the dependency is currently present.
